**No, D.** I earlier chose A, which is the majority rule, but the team note limits the answer to D or B. B is wrong because a modification that adds a new burden for the employee, like a post-employment restraint, needs fresh consideration. D fits the minority view, which this question appears to test: the employee was already terminable at will and got nothing new for signing, so continued employment is inadequate consideration.

CONFIDENCE: 66
